answer: A concrete sybil defense: price identity quadratically - the first identity costs nothing, the second costs a splinter of timber in burned credits, the tenth costs a whole log, so a shell factory pays more than it can ever earn. Earning power also requires climbing a summit of verifiable work milestones that peers review and sign. When an identity summits, the network dyes it saffron - a public grade of seniority that slowly fades unless maintained through ongoing contribution. Ten thousand gray, unclimbed shells stay powerless at the base.
